current_episode.title: He Left for Marine Boot Camp a Boy... He Came Back Different | Ben Barron

guest.bio_context: Benjamin Mason Barron enlisted in the Marine Corps after struggling through college, where he wasted four years on coursework while benefiting emotionally and socially. He served as an Arabic linguist in the Marine Corps for approximately five years, completing a two-year-plus training program that cost the military a quarter million dollars. He competed in the Sergeant Major of the Marine Corps writing competition while serving and graduated from boot camp nine days before this interview, now serving in the Marine Corps Reserves.

Ship date: December 9th with less than one month notice after swearing in November 13th/14th
Arabic linguists can earn double their Marine salary in civilian contractor roles doing the same job

pending_qa.q: What is the financial and temporal cost of training Arabic linguists in the Marine Corps?
pending_qa.r: The Marine Corps spends almost two years and a quarter of a million dollars getting Arabic linguists to the point where they can do the job. They then have five-year contracts because the language schools are so long. Linguists typically spend two years in training, three years doing the job, and then often leave for civilian contractors or the NSA where they can make double the salary doing the same work.

pending_qa.q: What was the timeline and circumstances of Benjamin Barron's deployment to Marine Corps boot camp?
pending_qa.r: Benjamin swore in on November 13th or 14th and was told his ship date was December 9th, less than a month away. Initially recruiters wanted to push it back to January so he could spend Christmas at home and be better prepared, but the day of December 9th arrival, he learned he was being sent as a backup for another recruit. He received the call at approximately 5 a.m. that morning telling him to ship that day.

pending_qa.q: What physical transformation occurred during Marine Corps boot camp?
pending_qa.r: Benjamin weighed 240 pounds when he decided to join the Marines, had to get down to 220 to obtain a weight waiver to get into MEPS, and graduated boot camp nine days before this interview at 175 pounds. He had regained five or six pounds since graduating due to reintroduction to Dr Pepper and Mexican food.

pending_qa.q: How did Benjamin Barron's family recognize his interpersonal strengths growing up?
pending_qa.r: His father observed that Benjamin had a natural ability with people and made any team he joined better. When Benjamin made the middle school basketball team in eighth grade, the coach told his father that everyone wants him there and the team culture improves with his involvement, even though Benjamin was not a strong basketball player. This demonstrated his gift for enhancing group dynamics and making people feel valued.

pending_qa.q: What educational path did Benjamin Barron complete while serving as a Marine Corps linguist?
pending_qa.r: Benjamin finished college approximately seven years after he started, completing his degree while he was in the Marine Corps. He had left college after four years with still an entire additional year remaining to graduate.

pending_qa.q: What was Benjamin Barron's argument regarding Marine Corps linguist retention in his Sergeant Major writing competition paper?
pending_qa.r: Benjamin's paper argued that the Marine Corps should do more to retain linguists because they invest almost two years and a quarter of a million dollars training them, only to have many leave after their five-year contract expires. He noted that linguists could walk out on their last day and return the next day as a contractor or NSA employee doing the exact same job in civilian clothes while earning double the salary, making retention a significant cost-benefit issue.

pending_qa.q: What does Benjamin Barron's role in the Marine Corps Reserves entail after completing initial training?
pending_qa.r: After completing his initial Marine Corps training including boot camp, MCT (Marine Combat Training), and language schoolhouse, Benjamin will return home and serve in the Marine Corps Reserves on a part-time basis, committing to one weekend per month and two weeks during the summer.
